LESSON: READING 10.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: CHARACTERS AND THEIR TRAITS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.4: Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Characters and their traits
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Characters and their traits, part of Strand 10 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why oral narratives in modern society? 2. What should one consider when collecting narratives among people of varied socio- cultural backgrounds?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 10.4.1 Intensive Reading: Characters and their traits together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: A learner discuss the lessons learned and the relevance of monster narratives in

real life.

● Learning to learn: Learner seeks support from resource persons on how to relate monsters to real life.

Values:
● Patriotism: A learner becomes conscious of their moral duties upon relating monster narratives to real life

● Responsibility: A learner learns to act responsibly since monsters represent evil in society responsibly.

Link to other subjects:

● Indigenous languages: monster narratives are part of oral literature, which is a key component of indigenous

languages.
